ATOMIC OPERATION MISMATCH (total drop)

The C program uses 3 atomic operation(s), but the Rust translation uses NONE.

C atomic operations:
  offset=0x130: 64-bit atomic add (fetch=True)
  offset=0x150: 64-bit atomic add (fetch=True)
  offset=0x270: 32-bit atomic add (fetch=True)

FIX INSTRUCTIONS:
You MUST use core::sync::atomic operations instead of plain pointer dereferences.

Required import:
  use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicU32, AtomicU64, Ordering};

Translation patterns:
  __sync_fetch_and_add(ptr, val) →
    unsafe { AtomicU32::from_ptr(ptr) }.fetch_add(val, Ordering::Relaxed)
  __sync_fetch_and_add(ptr, val) →
    unsafe { AtomicU64::from_ptr(ptr) }.fetch_add(val, Ordering::Relaxed)

Example (fetch_add):
  // C:    __sync_fetch_and_add(val, 1);
  // Rust: unsafe { AtomicU64::from_ptr(val) }.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
